root_cause_label: Insufficient Domain Knowledge of Redcode Assembly
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent repeatedly generated functionally broken Redcode warriors due to a fundamental misunderstanding of Redcode addressing modes and instruction semantics, resulting in 0% win rates for most attempts and never approaching the required win-rate thresholds against any of the five opponents.
t_err_evidence: agent rewrites warrior with broken djn-based scanner; labels and loop structure fundamentally incorrect
t_commit_evidence: After step 11, the agent cycles through the same broken scanner and replicator-bomber patterns (steps 13-58) without ever correctly implementing Redcode addressing, confirming the knowledge gap is irrecoverable within this trajectory. The best result (58 wins in step 44) was still far below the required 75%+ average across all five opponents, and the agent never even tested all opponents together.
t_surface_evidence: Results: 0 100 0 — zero wins after running new broken warrior design against stone.red
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks domain-specific knowledge of Redcode assembly semantics: it does not understand how Redcode addressing modes (@, <, >, }, *) work, that djn decrements a target instruction's B-field not a separate counter, or why mov bomb, @start bombs the warrior's own code. This gap persists throughout all 58 steps and prevents any viable warrior from being produced.
forewarning_evidence: Results: 0 79 21 — zero wins before rewrite, showing original warrior completely failing
